title: Behold Th' Amazing Sight
description: Behold Th' Amazing Sight in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 247 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Attraction of the Cross”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold th'a-maz-ing sight, The Sa-viour lift-ed high! Be-hold the Fa-ther's chief de-light Ex-pire in a-go-ny!

lines: For whom, for whom, my heart,
Why did he feel that piercing smart,
For love of us he bled,
'T was love that bowed his fainting head,
But from his cross pursue their flight

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
